title: Garlic Butter Steak Bites
subtitle: seared sirloin cubes tossed in garlic butter, with crispy roasted baby potatoes
imageAlt: Seared steak bites in garlic butter with golden roasted baby potatoes
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Frozen steak? Thaw in the fridge overnight. Take it out 20 minutes before cooking so it sears evenly.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) for the potatoes — they go in first.
Cut the steak into even 2.5 cm (1") cubes and pat them very dry — dry steak = brown crust.
Use your heaviest skillet (cast iron if you have it) and get it really hot. Turn on the fan!

steps.title: Roast the potatoes
steps.text: Toss the potatoes with oil, salt, garlic powder, paprika, Italian seasoning and pepper. Spread cut-side down on a sheet pan and roast at 220°C (425°F) for 30–35 minutes, flipping once, until crispy and tender. (Air fryer: 200°C / 400°F, 18–20 min, shaking twice.)

steps.title: Season the steak
steps.text: With 10 minutes left on the potatoes, pat the steak cubes very dry and toss with salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika.

steps.title: Sear in batches
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large heavy skillet over high until it just smokes. Add half the steak in one layer — don't crowd it. Sear 1–2 minutes without moving, then turn and cook 1–2 minutes more until browned. Move to a plate; repeat with the rest.

steps.title: Check doneness
steps.text: Steak bites cook fast, so check a thick piece with a thermometer: medium-rare 55–57°C (130–135°F), medium 60–63°C (140–145°F), medium-well 65–68°C (150–155°F). Health Canada's safe minimum for whole-muscle beef is 63°C (145°F). Pull them a couple of degrees early — they keep cooking.

steps.title: Garlic butter toss
steps.text: Turn the heat to medium-low. Melt the butter, add the garlic (and thyme) and cook 30–60 seconds until fragrant — don't let it burn. Return the steak and juices, add the soy sauce if using, and toss 30 seconds to coat.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Pile the steak bites next to the crispy potatoes and spoon over the garlic butter from the pan.

fixIt.fix: The pan wasn't hot enough or was crowded, so it steamed. Dry the steak well, heat the pan until it smokes, and cook in batches.
Overcooked, or the cubes were cut too big/uneven. Pull at your target temp; sirloin is best at medium-rare to medium.
The pan was still on high. Drop to medium-low before the butter and garlic go in — it only needs 30–60 seconds.
Give them space on the pan, cut-side down, and don't flip too early. An extra 5 minutes helps.

saleTip: Top sirloin is one of the best-value steaks at No Frills — often around $9.99/lb ($22/kg) on sale vs ~$12/lb regular. Buy a big pack and freeze 900 g portions.
swap: Use striploin for extra tenderness (pricier), or chicken thigh bites (cook to 74°C / 165°F).
leftovers: Fridge 3 days. Reheat steak gently (30 seconds at a time in the microwave, or quickly in a hot pan) so it doesn't overcook. Great sliced over rice for lunch.
doneness: Steak to your liking: medium-rare 55–57°C (130–135°F), medium 60–63°C (140–145°F), medium-well 65–68°C (150–155°F). Health Canada safe minimum: 63°C (145°F).
source: Based on tested steak bite methods (The Forked Spoon, The Meat Table): dry 1-inch cubes, very hot pan, batches, garlic butter finish.
prepAhead: Cube the steak up to a day ahead; keep covered in the fridge (pat dry before searing).
Halve the potatoes ahead and keep them in cold water; dry well before roasting.
reheat: Steak: very briefly — 30 seconds at a time in the microwave or 1 min in a hot pan — so it doesn't overcook. Potatoes: air fryer 190°C (375°F) for 5–6 min to re-crisp.

basic.note: Seared steak bites in garlic butter with simple roast potatoes.

stepNotes.1: Basic: salt, pepper and garlic powder.

fancy.note: Striploin bites with brown-butter garlic, crispy smashed potatoes and Parmesan.

stepNotes.0: Fancy: halfway through, press each potato flat with a glass and roast until crispy.
stepNotes.4: Fancy: let the butter brown and smell nutty before adding the garlic.

plating: Pile the steak bites high, glossy side up.
Smashed potatoes around, crispiest side showing.
Spoon the brown butter over just before serving.

why.1-0: Dry steak sears; damp steak steams grey.
why.2-0: The butter carries the garlic flavour over everything.
why.1-5: Very hot oil gives the crust — don't crowd the pan.
